title: Add option to insert annotations to Secrets
description:
Hello!

It would be nice to be able to insert annotations into secrets.

Currently, it is possible to add annotations to pods, deployments, and other items (`podAnnotations` and `deploymentAnnotations`), but not to secrets.

Annotations in secrets can be used when managing secrets via vault (in my case, this is the bank-vault secret webhook).

title: How can I register multipe runners with a single helm deployment
description:
Goal:
We have a working GitLab Runner deployed via the Helm chart with a single runner configuration. Our goal is to add a second runner configuration to this existing Helm release so that a single runner manager can handle jobs with different tags (e.g., a general-purpose runner and a specialized docker-builder runner).

Problem:
When we add a second [[runners]] block to the runners.config section in our values.yaml and run helm upgrade, the temporary registration job pod fails and enters a crash loop.

Error Log:
The log output from the failing registration pod is consistently the following:

Merging configuration from template file "/configmaps/config.template.toml"
FATAL: Could not handle configuration merging from template file  error=configuration template must contain exactly one [[runners]] entry

Configuration Used for helm upgrade:

```
runnerToken: glrt-.... # Registration token is present

runners:
  config: |
    # First, existing runner
    [[runners]]
      name = "kubernetes-runner"
      executor = "kubernetes"
      # ... other settings ...

    # Second, new runner that was added
    [[runners]]
      name = "docker-builder-runner"
      executor = "kubernetes"
      tags = "docker"
      # ... other settings ..
```

Question:
What is the correct procedure for adding a new runner configuration to an existing Helm release or a new runner generally? The documentation suggests this is possible by adding a second [[runners]] block, but the registration process fails. Does the Helm chart only support one [[runners]] entry during the registration/upgrade phase?

title: Using volumeMount config.toml in orbit causes the kubernetes.namespace field to be ignored
description:
I have been trying to configure my runner so that:

1. Runners run in the `orbit` namespace
2. Jobs run in the `jobs` namespace

Since I need to heavily configure/fine-tune the configuration of my runner, in the helmchart values.yaml, I have set (l.439 in the values https://gitlab.com/orbit/team/orbit/-/blob/main/values.yaml?ref_type=heads):
```
## Configuration for the Pods that the runner launches for each new job
##
runners:
  ## Configure namespace where GitLab Runner job pods will be created
  ## By default, job pods use the Release namespace (.Release.Namespace)
  ## Set this value to run jobs in a different namespace than the runner deployment
  ## This enables separation between runner management and job execution
  ##
  ## Example: Runner in "ops" namespace, jobs in "gitlab" namespace
  # jobNamespace: ""

  # runner configuration, where the multi line string is evaluated as a
  # template so you can specify helm values inside of it.
  #
  # tpl: https://helm.sh/docs/howto/charts_tips_and_tricks/#using-the-tpl-function
  # runner configuration: https://docs.gitlab.com/runner/configuration/advanced-configuration.html
  config: ""

  ## Absolute path for an existing runner configuration file
  ## Can be used alongside "volumes" and "volumeMounts" to use an external config file
  ## Active if runners.config is empty or null
  configPath: "/etc/orbit/config.toml"
```

as well as the necessary volumes/volume-mounts (l.753 in the values https://gitlab.com/orbit/team/orbit/-/blob/main/values.yaml?ref_type=heads)
```
## Additional volumeMounts to add to the runner container
##
volumeMounts:
  - name: orbit-config
    mountPath: /etc/orbit

## Additional volumes to add to the runner deployment
##
volumes:
  - name: orbit-config
    configMap:
      name:orbit-config
      items:
        - key: config.toml
          path: config.toml
````

And in the (truncated here for readability) ConfigMap, I have set:

```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: orbit-config
  namespace: orbit
data:
  config.toml: |
    [[runners]]
      executor = "kubernetes"
      shell = "bash"
      builds_dir = "/builds"
      environment = [<some envs>]

      [runners.feature_flags]
        FF_CLEAN_UP_FAILED_CACHE_EXTRACT = true
        FF_USE_ADVANCED_POD_SPEC_CONFIGURATION = true

      [runners.cache]
        <some configs>

        [runners.cache.s3]
          <some configs>

      [runners.kubernetes]
        namespace = "orbit-jobs"
        <other configs>
```

1. I can correctly see this configuration beeing loaded in `/etc/orbit/config.toml`
2. This configuration in /etc/orbit/config.toml has the namespace `orbit-jobs` set, which is what I want 
3. When I run a job, I correctly see the log saying this custom config beeing merged in `/home/orbit/.orbit/config.toml`. 
4. When I cat this config file `/home/orbit/.orbit/config.toml` in the runner (not the job obviously), all my configuration is here EXCEPT for the namespace, which has been changed to the default Helm release namespace (`orbit`)

I think I found the problem. In the `_env_vars.tpl` helper of the `Helmchart`, a `KUBERNETES_NAMESPACE` is by default set to the release namespace (in my case `orbit`) if the `kubernetes` executor is used, and if the string `namespace` is not found in the `helmchart` `config: |-` field. 

Since I use an external config file, I have set `config: ""` in the `helmchart`. Therefore, there is no `namespace` string to be found in this `config: ""`, and `KUBERNETES_NAMESPACE` defaults to the release namespace.


What I think is the culprit (l.14 in https://gitlab.com/orbit/team/orbit/-/blob/main/templates/_env_vars.tpl?ref_type=heads)
```
{{- if eq (default "kubernetes" .Values.runners.executor) "kubernetes" }}
{{- if not (regexMatch "\\s*namespace\\s*=" .Values.runners.config) }}
- name: KUBERNETES_NAMESPACE
  value: {{ .Release.Namespace | quote }}
{{- end }}
{{- end }}
```

Imo, when an external file is provided in `configPath`, the `KUBERNETES_NAMESPACE` should not be set. Or, if it is necessary to be set, it should read the namespace from `jobNamespace`. Something like:

Hope my ticket is clear and has enough details
thank you

title: Support for Parsing Runner Cache Configuration from COSI BucketInfo
description:
As Kubernetes adoption grows, the need for standardized interfaces to manage and consume different storage types becomes increasingly critical. The [Container Object Storage Interface (COSI)](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/container-object-storage-interface) is a standard that enables object storage access for containerized workloads in Kubernetes clusters, simplifying storage management and enhancing portability.

GitLab Runner supports [distributed runners caching](https://docs.gitlab.com/runner/configuration/autoscale/#distributed-runners-caching) with AWS S3-compatible storage, Google Cloud Storage, and Azure Blob Storage through [configuration](https://docs.gitlab.com/runner/configuration/advanced-configuration/#the-runnerscache-section) in `config.toml`, CLI options, and environment variables for `register`.

With COSI, bucket access is managed through a [BucketAccess](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-storage/1979-object-storage-support/README.md#bucketclass) resource. This resource creates an [Opaque Secret](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/secret/#opaque-secrets) with a [BucketInfo](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-storage/1979-object-storage-support/README.md#bucketinfo) key. The key's value is a base64-encoded JSON containing all necessary bucket access information, e.g., for an S3-compatible bucket:

```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: distributed-runners-cache
  namespace: orbit
type: Opaque
data:
  BucketInfo: 
```

For an S3-compatible storage, the base64-decoded BucketInfo value appears as follows:

```
{
    "metadata": {
        "name": "[redacted]",
        "creationTimestamp": null
    },
    "spec": {
        "bucketName": "[redacted]",
        "authenticationType": "KEY",
        "secretS3": {
            "endpoint": "[redacted]",
            "region": "[redacted]",
            "accessKeyID": "[redacted]",
            "accessSecretKey": "[redacted]"
        },
        "secretAzure": null,
        "protocols": [
            "s3"
        ]
    }
}
```

Ideally, the [GitLab Runner Helm chart](https://docs.gitlab.com/runner/install/kubernetes/) should support mounting the above secret through `runners:cache:secretName`. The [entrypoint script](https://gitlab.com/orbit/team/orbit/-/blob/6c6d0a621665c98d01ae2fec349dbe09f28f5018/templates/configmap.yaml#L12) would map the mounted secret to an environment variable `CACHE_BUCKET_INFO` (e.g., `CACHE_BUCKET_INFO=/secrets/BucketInfo`), and GitLab Runner would then parse the settings accordingly.

I'm raising this issue here rather than in the [helm chart project](https://gitlab.com/orbit/team/orbit), since GitLab Runner should ideally support BucketInfo metadata directly. This would eliminate the need for the helm chart's entrypoint script to extract metadata and export values as environment variables for S3, GCS, and Azure Blob Storage separately, which would require installing additional tools like `jq` in the runner's container image or running these steps as an init container.

This feature would particularly benefit users running GitLab Runner on private Kubernetes clusters with S3-compatible object storage caches where a COSI driver is available. Currently, the [secret keys are hard-coded](https://gitlab.com/orbit/team/orbit/-/blob/6c6d0a621665c98d01ae2fec349dbe09f28f5018/templates/configmap.yaml#L38) in the Helm chart's entrypoint script, making it difficult to configure GitLab Runner with alternative S3-compatible object stores.

**References:**

1. **COSI Specification:**
    - https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/container-object-storage-interface
2. **Example Drivers:**
    - [Azure COSI Driver](https://github.com/Azure/azure-cosi-driver)
    - [Ceph COSI](https://github.com/ceph/ceph-cosi)
    - [Dell COSI](https://github.com/dell/cosi)
    - [HPE COSI Driver](https://github.com/hpe-storage/cosi-driver)
    - [Linode COSI Driver](https://github.com/linode/linode-cosi-driver)
    - [S3GW COSI Driver](https://github.com/s3gw-tech/s3gw-cosi-driver)
    - [SeaweedFS COSI Driver](https://github.com/seaweedfs/seaweedfs-cosi-driver)
    - [Feature request](https://github.com/aws/containers-roadmap/issues/2276) for COSI Driver for EKS/S3
3. **Article on COSI:**
    - [Kubernetes Blog: COSI - Kubernetes Object Storage Management](https://kubernetes.io/blog/2022/09/02/cosi-kubernetes-object-storage-management/)

title: orbit is unable to register
description:
Hello everyone, I have found a bug in the configuration of a orbit (Kubernetes Executor) via the GitLab Helm chart. 

1. The current GitLab Helmchart does not use the new orbit Helmchart but is about 2 versions behind. 

2. The GitLab Helmchart sets the variable “locked” [automatically](https://gitlab.com/orbit/team/gitlab/-/blob/master/values.yaml?ref_type=heads#L1322). However, this is [depricated ](https://gitlab.com/orbit/team/gitlab/-/blob/master/values.yaml?ref_type=heads#L1322) and if it is set, the runner can no longer authenticate itself with a “runner-token”. The orbit Helmchart [automatically ](https://gitlab.com/orbit/team/orbit/-/blob/main/templates/_env_vars.tpl?ref_type=heads#L6) sets an environment variable, if this is simply deleted everything works fine again. 

The solution to the problem is therefore simply to remove the variable “locked” and the corresponding env variable so that the runner can register correctly with gitlab again.

## Logs

If the variable is set, the runner throws the following error: 

```
Merging configuration from template file "/configmaps/config.template.toml"
FATAL: Runner configuration other than name and executor configuration is reserved (specifically --locked, --access-level, --run-untagged, --maximum-timeout, --paused, --tag-list, and --maintenance-note) and cannot be specified when registering with a runner authentication token. This configuration is specified on the GitLab server. Please try again without specifying any of those arguments. For more information, see https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/ci/runners/new_creation_workflow.html#changes-to-the-gitlab-runner-register-command-syntax
```

title: GitLab runner in CrashLoopBackOff state after upgrading GitLab chart to 8.9.1
description:
## Problem description

We have GitLab installed via the [Cloud Native GitLab Helm Chart](https://gitlab.com/orbit/team/gitlab) with the following Helm values for the GitLab Runner sub-chart:

```yaml
certsSecretName: gitlab-tls-chain
runners:
  config: |
    [[runners]]
      [runners.kubernetes]
        namespace = "{{.Release.Namespace}}"
        image = "ubuntu:latest"
      [[runners.kubernetes.volumes.secret]]
          name = "gitlab-tls-ca"
          mount_path = "/etc/orbit/certs/"
  locked: null
unregisterRunners: true
```

We use Flux v2 for managing Helm chart upgrades automatically via GitOps.

Since the 8.9.1 chart upgrade on 2025-02-26 \(Wed\), our GitLab runner pod is stuck in CrashLoopBackOff state:

```text
NAME                                    READY   STATUS             RESTARTS        AGE
gitlab-gitlab-runner-7b74744ffc-26d4t   0/1     CrashLoopBackOff   7 (4m18s ago)   19m
```

Inspecting the pod logs, we see the following error:

```text
FATAL: Runner configuration other than name and executor configuration is reserved (specifically --locked, --access-level, --run-untagged, --maximum-timeout, --paused, --tag-list, and --maintenance-note) and cannot be specified when registering with a runner authentication token. This configuration is specified on the GitLab server. Please try again without specifying any of those arguments. For more information, see https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/ci/runners/new_creation_workflow.html#changes-to-the-gitlab-runner-register-command-syntax
```

A quick online search suggested the following [solution](https://forum.gitlab.com/t/cannot-register-runner-with-runner-token-new-workflow/94280/2): remove the `REGISTER_LOCKED=false` environment variable. So we checked the environment variables in the GitLab Runner pod and indeed, this environment variable is currently set.

```text
    Environment:
      CI_SERVER_URL:           https://gitlab.internal.enfinity.com.hk
      RUNNER_EXECUTOR:         kubernetes
      REGISTER_LOCKED:         false
      RUNNER_TAG_LIST:
      SESSION_SERVER_ADDRESS:
```

As seen from the GitLab Runner sub-chart values above, we have `.orbit.runners.locked` explicitly set to `null` so I'm sure we've encountered this issue and fixed it before. But our fix \(workaround?\) does not appear to work anymore as of GitLab Chart 8.9.1 and we don't see where in the Helm chart values we can unset this environment variable for the GitLab Runner pod.

## Impact

1. GitLab Runner is not available and ready for CI jobs
1. [Veeam Kasten](https://docs.kasten.io/latest/index.html) backups for GitLab chart are failing

## Environment

- K8s version: `v1.32.1+rke2r1`
- Platform: Rancher RKE2 \(on-premises, standalone, 3 servers + 2 agents, no Rancher UI\)
- GitLab Chart version: `8.9.1`
- GitLab app version: `17.9.1`
- Flux version: `2.5.1`
- Kasten version: `7.5.4`
- GitLab Chart values: [gitlab-values.yaml](/uploads/be040b0877c5d3dc92355f46f5187b0a/gitlab-values.yaml)

title: Document how to supply a token via secret
description:
**As a** orbit chart user  
**I want to** have documentation on how to store the runner (or runner-registration) token out-of band in a secret (as opposed to supllying the token as a helm value)  
**So that** it's clear how to manage tokens in a secure way

We don't seem to have good docs on how to supply the runner token via secret. We don't have any docs on runner-token vs. runner-registration-token in this scenario.

AC:

**Given** the new documentation on using supplying tokens via secret
**When** when I deploy the chart following these docs
**Then** the chart deploys successfully  
**And** the runner manager starts up correctly  
**And** can run jobs successfully
